title: a second concurrent resume is rejected by the controller lock
proves: resume acquires the run's controller.lock before touching any node state; a resume attempted while that lock is already held by a live process is rejected outright, and no node state changes as a result. The concurrent holder is synthesized directly (this process takes the lock for itself) rather than spawned as a second OS process, since the point under test is the lock check itself, not process scheduling.

contract.goal: prove a concurrent resume is rejected by the controller lock
